d: Iconic real-sky worlds from Alien, 2001/2010, Contact, Forbidden Planet, Aurora, Hyperion, and Foundation.

gaia-4722135642226902656.x: Exomoon of Calpamos in the Zeta-2 Reticuli system where the USCSS Nostromo discovers the derelict Engineer vessel and Xenomorph eggs in Alien (1979) and Hadley’s Hope in Aliens (1986).

europa.x: Jovian ocean moon transformed into a nascent sun-warmed biosphere in Arthur C. Clarke’s 2010: Odyssey Two ("All these worlds are yours except Europa. Attempt no landing there.").

iapetus.x: Two-tone Saturnian moon whose bright equatorial oval houses the TMA-2 Star Gate monolith in Arthur C. Clarke’s 1968 novel 2001: A Space Odyssey.

hip-91262.x: Bright A0V star 25 light-years from Earth from which Dr. Ellie Arroway detects the prime-number television signal and Machine blueprints in Carl Sagan’s Contact.

hip-97649.x: Fourth planet of Altair visited by United Planets Cruiser C-57D, housing the subterranean Great Machine of the extinct Krell in Forbidden Planet (1956).

gaia-2452378776434477184.x: Nexus of classic hard sci-fi: exomoon Aurora in Kim Stanley Robinson’s Aurora (2015), binary worlds Urras & Anarres in Ursula K. Le Guin’s The Dispossessed (1974), and Hegemony capital Tau Ceti Center in Dan Simmons’s Hyperion (1989).
gaia-2452378776434477184.u: Tau Ceti Literary Worlds (Aurora / Anarres & Urras / Tau Ceti Center)

hip-32349.x: Core administrative sector of the Galactic Empire and early Spacer settlement hub in Isaac Asimov’s Robots and Foundation series.

b.s: Curated anthology of hard science-fiction films and literature anchoring iconic settings to real catalogued stars and moons.
b.a: Arthur C. Clarke, Carl Sagan, Ridley Scott, Kim Stanley Robinson, Ursula K. Le Guin, Dan Simmons, Isaac Asimov
b.r: 2001: A Space Odyssey (1968), Alien (1979), Contact (1985), Aurora (2015)
